ctPredict

Source: R/ctKalman.R
ctPredict.Rd

Outputs predicted, updated, and smoothed estimates of manifest indicators and latent states, with covariances, for specific subjects from data fit with ctFit, based on either the mode (if optimized) or mean (if sampled) of parameter distribution. ctKalman is an alias for this function. ctStanKalman, despite the similar name, is an alias for ctKalmanArray, which returns a list of arrays.

Usage

ctPredict(
  fit,
  timerange = "asdata",
  timestep = "auto",
  subjects = NULL,
  removeObs = FALSE,
  plot = FALSE,
  standardisederrors = FALSE,
  realid = TRUE,
  randomEffects = NULL,
  newdata = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

fit

fit object as generated by ctFit.

timerange

Either 'asdata' to just use the observed data range, or a numeric vector of length 2 denoting start and end of time range, allowing for estimates outside the range of observed data. Ranges smaller than the observed data are ignored.

timestep

Either 'asdata' to just use the observed data (which also requires 'asdata' for timerange) or a positive numeric value indicating the time step to use for interpolating values. Lower values give a more accurate / smooth representation, but take a little more time to calculate.

subjects

subject ids to predict for, or NULL (the default) for the first subject in the data, or every subject in newdata when that is given. With realid=FALSE, integers denoting subjects from 1 to N.

removeObs

Logical or integer. If TRUE, observations (but not covariates) are withheld from the filter, so only expectations based on parameters and covariates are returned (the observations themselves are still reported, for comparison). If a positive integer N, every N observations are retained while others are withheld – useful for observing prediction performance forward further in time than one observation.

plot

Logical. If TRUE, plots output instead of returning it. See plot.ctKalmanDF (Stan based fit) for the possible arguments.

standardisederrors

if TRUE, also include standardised error output (based on covariance per time point).

realid

If TRUE (the default), subjects are read as the ids in the data, and integers that are not ids there are read as ctsem's numbering of the subjects, 1 to N, with a message. If FALSE, they are read as that numbering.

randomEffects

For an intoverpop='laplace' fit, which levels of random effects the trajectories include. Naming one of the model's id columns includes that level and all levels above it, so the innermost id gives each subject its own trajectory, and an outer id gives the group mean, shared by the subjects in the group. 'population' includes none, giving the trajectory implied by the population parameters alone. Defaults to the innermost id. Ignored for other fits.

With a single level of random effects included, each subject's predicted and updated values use the posterior of its random effects given its observations up to each time, and its smoothed values use their mode given its whole record. Otherwise all values use the modes given each subject's whole record. These modes are those of the fit, and do not change when this call changes which rows are filtered (selected subjects, a time grid, removeObs). So with every observation withheld, the smoothed values still use the subject's own random effects.

newdata

Optional long format data to predict for instead of the data the model was fitted to, with the same columns: an id, a time, the manifest variables (NA where nothing is observed) and the predictors. It can hold new subjects, such as hypothetical people with chosen covariate values, a subject of the fit with other covariate values, or a record cut short at some time, to see what could be predicted then. The fit's estimates are used without refitting, and the model structure is kept for any number of subjects. A subject's predicted (prior) and updated values are conditional on its rows in newdata up to each time, and its smoothed values on all of its rows. For a fit with random effects this includes the subject's random effects (as estimated from those rows for a Laplace fit with one level of random effects, and otherwise as randomEffects describes), so a subject with no observations gets the population's prediction for its covariate values. A row with nothing observed gives a prediction at that time. A time dependent predictor left NA is taken as zero, as in ctFit.

...

additional arguments to pass to plot.ctKalmanDF.

Value

Returns a list containing matrix objects etaprior, etaupd, etasmooth, y, yprior, yupd, ysmooth, errprior, errupd, errsmooth, time, loglik, with values for each time point in each row. eta refers to latent states and y to manifest indicators - y itself is thus just the input data. With standardisederrors=TRUE, standardised versions errstdprior, errstdupd, errstdsmooth are included too. Covariance matrices etapriorcov, etaupdcov, etasmoothcov, ypriorcov, yupdcov, ysmoothcov, are returned in a row * column * time array. Some outputs are unavailable for ctStan fits at present. If plot=TRUE, nothing is returned but a plot is generated.

Examples

# \donttest{

#Basic
ctPredict(ctstantestfit, timerange=c(0,60), plot=TRUE)

#Multiple subjects, y and yprior, showing plot arguments
plot1<-ctPredict(ctstantestfit, timerange=c(0,60), timestep=.1, plot=TRUE,
  subjects=2:3, 
  kalmanvec=c('y','yprior'),
  errorvec=c(NA,'ypriorcov')) #'auto' would also have achieved this
  
 #modify plot as per normal with ggplot
 print(plot1+ggplot2::coord_cartesian(xlim=c(0,10)))
 
 #or generate custom plot from scratch:#'  
 k=ctPredict(ctstantestfit, timerange=c(0,60), timestep=.1, subjects=2:3)
 library(ggplot2)
 ggplot(k[k$Element %in% 'yprior',],
   aes(x=Time, y=value,colour=Subject,linetype=Row)) +
   geom_line() +
   theme_bw()

#New subjects: two hypothetical people differing only in TI1, each
#observed once at time 0, predicted to time 4.
newsubjects <- data.frame(id = c('lowTI1', 'highTI1'), time = 0,
  Y1 = 8, Y2 = 12, TD1 = 0, TI1 = c(-1, 1))
newsubjects <- rbind(newsubjects,
  transform(newsubjects, time = 4, Y1 = NA, Y2 = NA))
k <- ctPredict(ctstantestfit, newdata = newsubjects, timerange = c(0, 4),
  timestep = .1)
k[k$Element %in% 'yprior' & k$Time == 4, ]
ctPredict(ctstantestfit, newdata = newsubjects, timerange = c(0, 4),
  timestep = .1, plot = TRUE, kalmanvec = 'yprior', errorvec = 'ypriorcov')
 # }
